subject: Clarification: startup behavior for streaming vs batch endpoints — ArgoHealth POC
messages:
From: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@argohealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@argohealth.com>, procurement@argohealth.com
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Streaming startup and sustained throughput for ArgoHealth POC

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the great demo last week. We're preparing the internal POC acceptance criteria and have one set of questions around the guarantees for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints. The RFP attached asks for explicit commitments for: 

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations for streaming responses (95th percentile)
- Sustained token/sec per connection under typical doc-parsing load (500–2,000 token responses)
- Fallback behavior if streaming cannot meet the TTFT target (does the system serve a full sync response?)

Our security/procurement folks want to understand any carve-outs we should expect (cold starts, model warm-up, quantized variants). Can you point us to how Redwood measures TTFT and what exceptions you would request for a targeted POC period?

Attached: ArgoHealth_RFP.pdf — section 4.2 lists the SLAs we need to map.

Best,
Elena Suarez
Head of Integrations, ArgoHealth
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@argohealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming startup and sustained throughput for ArgoHealth POC

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. High-level response up front: we can meet tight TTFT targets for the majority of POC traffic but need to document acceptable cold-start carve-outs and measurement methodology.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-min sync (this week) with Rishi to align measurement and warm-up expectations.
2) We ship a one-page exception letter for the POC that explains when streaming TTFT may slip (cold model load, region failover) and the fallback (sync whole-response).
3) Draft SLA mapping for procurement that maps each RFP item to Redwood metrics and compensating controls (tracing, trace-id correlation, dashboards).

I've looped in Rishi (serving/runtime) and Marissa (contracts) to propose specific wording. Can you do 10:30AM PT on Tuesday?

—Naomi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@argohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming startup and sustained throughput for ArgoHealth POC

Elena / Naomi — quick technical note ahead of the sync. We want the POC agreement to be measurable and operationally safe. A recommended approach we use with customers:

Measurement definitions (proposal):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): measured from request arrival at the Redwood edge to first byte emitted at the client, reported at 95th percentile over a 1,000-request sliding window.
- Sustained token/sec: measured per-connection over the active response window, median and 95th reported over a 10-minute sampling period under representative workload (we recommend running an rps profile that reflects your doc size distribution).

Reasonable carve-outs to document:
- Cold-starts: model weights paged-in or node spin-up may cause TTFT to exceed target for short windows during scale-up. We propose a 5-minute warm-up window per new capacity event.
- Variant mismatch: quantized or smaller model variants can change token/sec expectations; call out model family and quantization profile in the SLA appendix.
- Regional failover / maintenance windows: maintenance/failover events will be disclosed via status.redwood.ai and excluded from uptime calculations if declared.

Fallback behavior: when streaming cannot meet the TTFT target due to cold conditions, Redwood can automatically fall back to a sync full-response endpoint (same model family) that guarantees final response delivery. We typically include the fallback as an operational mitigation rather than a SLA credit trigger.

I've attached a first-pass draft that maps your RFP rows to our recommended metrics and exception language: redwood_streaming_guarantee_draft_v1.pdf and a short spreadsheet describing measurement hooks (startup-measurement-spec.xlsx).

I'll be ready to walk this through on the sync.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@argohealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@argohealth.com>, procurement@argohealth.com
Date: 2027-05-31T10:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming startup and sustained throughput for ArgoHealth POC

Thanks Rishi — that level of specificity helps. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/security:

- Can the warm-up window be shorter for small-scale POC (e.g., 1–2 minutes) if we run a scripted warm-up traffic burst?
- For the fallback to sync full-response: will you preserve the same model semantics/embedding/metadata so we don't get drift between streaming and sync outputs?
- We need clear telemetry hooks and a recommended query plan for our engineers to reproduce the measurement (headers, trace-id, sample payload).

If you can provide a short exception letter that states the POC carve-outs and measurements we'll route it through procurement. Ideally that letter is on Redwood letterhead and signed by an exec or legal.

Elena
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@argohealth.com>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@argohealth.com>, procurement@argohealth.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming startup and sustained throughput for ArgoHealth POC — proposed letter and MAP

Elena / team — thanks again for moving quickly on this. Attached is a concise exception letter and a mutual action plan (MAP) we can sign to get the POC moving:

Key points in the letter (high level):
- TTFT target: Redwood agrees to a 95th percentile TTFT of <= 350ms for streaming for the specified model family when served from warm pool nodes.
- POC carve-out: a documented 3-minute warm-up window per scale event for this POC if ArgoHealth agrees to run the signed warm-up script (we include instructions in the MAP).
- Sustained throughput: for the selected model variant (rwd-3b-fp16) we guarantee median sustained token/sec >= 140 and 95th >= 90 under the representative load profile; appendix lists measurement method.
- Fallback: automatic sync fallbacks preserve same model family and deterministic decoding seed for parity; we include guidance on drift risk in the appendix.
- Monitoring: we will enable a temporary dashboard for ArgoHealth (rdw-argo-poc) and provide a trace-id header to correlate requests to traces.

Next steps we propose:
1) ArgoHealth reviews/requests edits to the letter by EOD Thursday.
2) Procurement countersigns the MAP and we provision the dashboard.
3) Run warm-up script and a 2-hour soak; report back on baseline metrics.

Links: HubSpot deal ARGH-2027-045 (https://hubspot.com/deal/ARGH-2027-045) and the measurement spec in Drive (https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/argohealth-poc-docs).

If that looks good I'll get Marissa to route the letter to Legal for a signature.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
